assessment.overall_rationale: The strongest concordance is the shared NRP1–CDC42/CXCR4/ANGPT2 tip-cell program, while TGF-β modules overlap mainly in vascular remodeling and the flow-sensing module is largely setting-level context.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe an ANGPT2/CXCR4-positive endothelial tip-cell state in which NRP1 activates CDC42-dependent filopodial guidance during brain-vessel sprouting.
The modules share postnatal cerebrovascular maturation context, but tip-cell migration and filopodia are mechanistically distinct from potassium-channel-mediated flow sensing.
Both support endothelial migration and angiogenesis, but one specifies tip-cell guidance whereas the other centers on anti-apoptotic and metabolic support.
Both connect CXCR4, Notch-associated arterial specification, NRP1, and TEK to sprouting, although the left module more specifically emphasizes the tip-to-arterial or stalk transition.
They meet only in the broad context of postnatal vascular maturation, with no supplied mechanistic link between Dll4–Notch fate specification and KCNJ2 flow sensing.
Both concern angiogenic remodeling and include supportive TGF-β signaling, but arterial fate coupling differs from survival and metabolic fueling.
Both involve ANGPT2-dependent vascular remodeling, but the left centers on TGF-β-mediated integrity and ANGPT2 restraint while the right centers on ANGPT2-driven vessel destabilization and sprouting.
Aside from cerebrovascular maturation context, TGF-β/ANGPT2 control of integrity is distinct from KCNJ2-mediated mechanotransduction and vasodilation.

Both assign TGFBR1/TGFBR2 a positive role in vascular development and remodeling, but the principal mechanisms and predicted phenotypes are integrity and hemorrhage versus survival and metabolic angiogenic capacity.
